title: C649 — RH interior front door handle ambient lighting lamp connector
introduction:
I read this right-hand door-handle lamp reference from identity to location to purpose. Check the identification table, locate a cavity label in the drawing, then follow that label into the pin-assignment table. Read the circuit identifier alongside its function and colour entry so a familiar-looking wire does not send you down the wrong path.

The lamp name tells only part of the story: the table also includes passenger-latch unlock and lock-status indicator functions. Think of the connector as a small shared doorway for lighting and lock-related connections. Sharing the doorway does not make their jobs interchangeable.

Use this page for connector identification, circuit-map reading and service-part lookup. Physical access, release, viewing side, probing, electrical test conditions and replacement require a separate procedure. Gauge conventions and the catalogue codes under Box, Cols, Size and Used are undefined here; preserve them without treating them as dimensions, wire-selection instructions or evidence of a fault.

edits.why: The cavity labels occupy paired columns, and the housing projection sits on the right of the illustrated housing. I use those visible features as landmarks when moving between drawing and table. They orient the page without establishing a terminal-side or wire-side view of the actual connector.

Each Cavity entry ties a position in the drawing to its circuit identifier, colour, gauge, function and terminal reference. The lighting descriptions separate colour-channel positive connections from the LED negative connection; passenger-latch unlock and lock-status indication have their own rows. Retain the lighting zone or non-zone wording when interpreting a row. The LED negative label alone is not permission to treat that connection as chassis ground.

A pigtail combines a connector with attached wire leads. The kit, service-part and engineering-shell fields identify related service items, while individual terminal references appear in the pin table. I keep the pigtail lead specification distinct from the vehicle-wire specifications. A catalogue match helps identify a candidate part; it does not supply replacement, splicing or verification instructions.
